title: Soft-Body Duck Gear Press
description: A squishy rubber duck sits atop a mechanical gear press. The user manipulates interlocking gears to compress, stretch, and reshape the soft-body duck while conserving its total volume. An undo/redo system tracks each deformation step, and multiple gear inputs couple together to produce complex squish patterns.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load Duck.glb as a soft-body object and gears.glb as a mechanical press apparatus. Scene setup: place the gears model horizontally as a base platform with two vertical gear-driven press plates on the left and right sides, and a third gear-driven plate descending from above. Position the duck centered between the plates on the gear platform. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 5) looking at origin, with OrbitControls for viewing. Add ambient light (intensity 0.5), a directional light from (5, 10, 7), and a hemisphere light for soft fill. Implement soft-body simulation for the duck by treating its geometry vertices as a mass-spring system: on each frame, apply forces from the press plates to nearby vertices, displacing them inward, while an internal pressure force preserves total mesh volume (volume conservation law). Add a UI panel with: three sliders labeled 'Left Press', 'Top Press', 'Right Press' each ranging 0-100 controlling how far each gear plate advances toward the duck. Gear rotation should animate proportionally to slider values, visually turning the gears model. Multi-input coupling: when two or more presses engage simultaneously, the duck bulges outward in the unconstrained direction more aggressively (coupled response). Display current duck volume as a percentage of original volume (should stay near 100% due to conservation). Implement an interaction history stack supporting Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Redo (Ctrl+Y) that records each slider change as a discrete step. Show step counter (target: 10-14 meaningful interactions to fully explore all compression combinations). Add a 'Reset Duck' button that animates the duck back to its original shape. The duck should jiggle with damped oscillation after each press change. Color the duck bright yellow with a glossy material and give the gears a metallic PBR appearance.
